attribution.note: Zitron states this in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the appearance hedge and exclusivity claim; the surrounding context identifies Claude.

contract.note: The contract fairly preserves the hedge. A binary verdict would require an added definition of availability and a threshold for the claimed appearance.

evidence.note: Contemporary Reuters reporting explains the stated appearance, but its February account does not establish exclusivity on March 3.
OpenAI's company disclosure establishes an announced classified deployment agreement before the statement, but does not establish operational availability. It complicates an approval-based reading.

reviews.rationale: The appearance hedge does not commit Zitron to firm exclusivity. Availability also lacks a defined test. The reporting and competing deployment agreement provide context, but cannot turn the qualified statement into a scoreable binary claim.
